{{Quote|I can't even see the enemy!''"<br />"''That's why they're called the Shadow People, Tup!|Clone troopers during the Battle of Umbara|<ref name="DoU">{{TCW|Darkness on Umbara}}</ref>}}
'''Umbarans''', culturally known as the '''Shadow People''', resided on the dark world of [[Umbara/Legends|Umbara]] deep within the [[Ghost Nebula/Legends|Ghost Nebula]]. Umbarans could see in [[Ultraviolet/Legends|ultraviolet]] (below 300 nanometers) and had the ability to read, subtly influence, and sometimes control the will of others.

==Biology and appearance==
Umbarans were gaunt, frighteningly pale [[near-Human]]s with achromatic sunken eyes. Male Umbarans stand between 1.7 to 2.0 meters tall.<ref name="Galaxy of Intrigue" /> Due to Umbara's eternal twilight, their eyes were well adjusted to the dark, but they were easily disoriented when exposed to sudden bright flashes of light.<ref name="ua" />

==Society and Culture==
Umbarans spoke the language [[Umbarese/Legends|Umbarese]]<ref name="Galaxy of Intrigue" /> which was written using the [[Umbara alphabet/Legends|Umbaran alphabet]].<ref name="Darkness on Umbara">{{TCW|Darkness on Umbara}}</ref> Umbarans were highly isolated and manipulative. Many had a darker sense of humor than the average [[Human/Legends|Human]], which would manifest in social interactions. Masters of misdirection, Umbarans almost never revealed their true thoughts or intentions.<ref name="ua" />

Umbaran society was built on a finely detailed caste system comprising almost one hundred levels. Only those in the top ten caste levels were given the opportunity to leave their homeworld, explaining their rarity outside the Ghost Nebula.<ref name="Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> The primary ambition of the average Umbaran was to ascend through the caste levels, using tactics from blackmail and subterfuge to assassination. Assassination was attempted quite often and was done through sublte methods such as microscopic poison darts, nanotechnology, undetectable poisons, and small, stylish stiletto-like knives called vootkar. Shadowcloaks could be worn to further assist in these assassinations. These more subtle methods were seen as being more refined than blasters and vibroblades which were thought to be messy. Failed plots to ascend the ranks of society were met harshly with the attempted perpetrator imprisoned and their family dropped to one of the lower caste levels. Dependent upon the rank of the targeted individual, the perpetrator risked a [[Death/Legends|death]] sentence for themselves and their entire family. Successful maneuvering, however, was rewarded with prestige, making Umbarans view such attempts as being worth the risk.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

The highest caste level, known as [[Rootai]], comprised a council that ruled Umbara, and its members were considered royalty.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> The Umbarans had their own military known as the [[Umbaran militia]], which protected Umbara and the Umbarans from invasions.<ref name="The General">{{TCW|The General (episode)}}</ref>

==History==
Umbarans maintained a political presence starting with the dawn of the Old Republic, and during the era, they drifted like specters through Senate Corridors and various chambers of power.<ref name="ua" /> They became objects of fear and suspicion because of their subtle ability to influence others.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

During the [[Rise of the Empire era|waning years of the Old Republic]], Umbarans used their natural mental sway to secure positions of power. [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] selected an Umbaran by the name of [[Sly Moore/Legends|Sly Moore]] to be his [[Senior Administrative Aide/Legends|Staff Aide]]. Moore was entrusted with some of the soon-to-be [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor's]] darker secrets.<ref name="ua" /> 

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Umbarans seceded to the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] following the murder of Umbaran [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Mee Deechi/Legends|Mee Deechi]].<ref name="Darkness on Umbara" />

During the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], Umbarans were used as spies and thought police, with the [[Order 66/Legends|main objective]] of weeding out rogue [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] who escaped the onslaught.<ref name="ua" />

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Umbarans led the effort to root out potential traitors to the Emperor. Their effectiveness led even the Emperor's most dedicated followers to fear them, strengthening the [[Speciesism|xenophobic]] sentiment among many of his closest advisors. They assisted the Emperor in finding [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel sympathizers]] hiding within the ranks of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial government]] and military.<ref name="ua" /> The Umbarans were particularly disliked by officers of [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]], who resented the fact that they were subject to Umbaran scrutiny-a resentment that grew every time they unmasked a Rebel double agent in their ranks.<ref name="Galaxy of Intrigue" /> 

The [[Death/Legends|death]] of the Emperor at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] caught many Umbarans by surprise. Even before the fall of the Empire, Umbarans had already begun their retreat from the galaxy. Fearing retribution from both the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] and the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the Umbarans fled civilized space back to the Ghost Nebula.<ref name="ua" /> With time, as memories of the Empire started to fade in the minds of the galaxy's beings, the Umbarans began to filter back into the galaxy, though in the low numbers typical of their off-world presence during the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]].<ref name="Galaxy of Intrigue" />

Umbarans often wore [[Shadowcloak (clothing)|Shadowcloaks]].<ref name="ua" />
